brief: GS data show positioning near historic lows heading into Q3 earnings. Hedge fund US net positioning sits in the 0th percentile, Russell 2000 systematic exposure in the 7th percentile, and leveraged funds hold record Russell shorts (CFTC data, through September 22). The GS Monetary Policy Factor sits at -8, near the bottom of its 30-year range, reflecting extreme policy pessimism, yet volatility has stayed calm and equities have not cracked. Non-dealers sold $63.7bn of S&P futures over six weeks, selling five of six weeks ($10.5bn the latest week, $11.7bn from asset managers). More than 70% of the move was long liquidation, not new shorts. Asset-manager gross longs now move inversely with 10-year real yields, and a recent 25bp yield jump drove $5.5bn more liquidation, making a real-yield reversal the key upside trigger. Tech was the week's most-sold global sector, led by semis in EM Asia and Europe, though longer-term Tech allocations remain in the 96th percentile. Since September 29, softer PCE and payrolls have helped unwind about $900mn of Russell open interest and richen RTY funding spreads. Thesis: if real yields roll over and MOVE, now stabilizing, stays contained, this defensive positioning unwinds into earnings, turning the pain trade into a rally.
